_sources: Loaded by ui/main-panel/agents/agent-loop/js/loop-node-data.js → consumed by ui/main-panel/agents/agent-loop/js/loop-logic.js (panel rendering, loop diagram) and ui/main-panel/agents/js/agents.js (agent config panel)

user_input.name: /optimize
user_input.desc: Run the optimizer on this session to improve agent skills

user_input.name: /optimize <feedback>
user_input.desc: Run optimizer with specific feedback about what to improve

slash_cmd.name: /optimize [feedback]
slash_cmd.desc: Intercepts /optimize before the agent loop — runs optimizer directly

ensure_session.name: Settings → Sessions
ensure_session.desc: Creates a new session record if one does not already exist for this request

agent_resolve.name: Settings → Agent
agent_resolve.desc: Configure agent template, system prompt, and max turns

save_user_msg.name: Settings → Source
save_user_msg.desc: User message is persisted to the interactions table before the loop starts

load_context.name: Settings → Agent
load_context.desc: Edit context documents (agent, user, skills, tools, tasks sections)

copy_defaults.name: Settings → Agent
copy_defaults.desc: Default context is seeded from the default template on first run

skip_gate.name: Settings → Agent
skip_gate.desc: Short/trivial messages skip memory_search entirely (regex skip gate)

memory_search.name: Settings → Source
memory_search.desc: View and manage memory pages used for brain context injection

attachment_describe.name: App Config → Default LLM
attachment_describe.desc: Set per-model Text/Image capability and pick the image describer model

build_prompt.name: Settings → Agent
build_prompt.desc: Edit the agent's core directive, persona, and context sections

build_history.name: Settings → Source
build_history.desc: View session history — internal tools (memory_search/save) are stripped

load_provider.name: Settings → Provider
load_provider.desc: Configure LLM base URL, API key, model, and parallel providers

load_tools.name: Settings → Agent
load_tools.desc: Configure which tools are enabled or disabled for this agent

integration_status.name: Settings → Integrations
integration_status.desc: Enable OAuth integrations for this agent in the Integrations tab

interrupt_chk.name: Settings → Agent
interrupt_chk.desc: _check_interrupt() — checked at the start of every while-loop turn

turn_counter.name: Settings → Max Turns
turn_counter.desc: Increments turn counter; exits loop if max_turns exceeded

permission_chk.name: Settings → Max Turns
permission_chk.desc: At turn 11+ the agent requests permission to continue — configurable via fragments

build_tool_defs.name: Settings → Agent
build_tool_defs.desc: Converts loaded tool metadata into the LLM tool_calls schema format

llm_call.name: Settings → Provider
llm_call.desc: Change the LLM model, base URL, or API key

llm_call.name: Settings → Agent
llm_call.desc: Edit the agent's system prompt and persona

db_persist_asst.name: Settings → Source
db_persist_asst.desc: Assistant message (with tool_calls suffix) is saved to DB before validation runs

validate_tools.name: Settings → Agent
validate_tools.desc: _validate_tool_call() — checks tool name exists and args are valid

destructive_chk.name: Settings → Agent
destructive_chk.desc: DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS set: edit_source, write_source, delete_source, run_command, restart_server

post_val_chk.name: Settings → Agent
post_val_chk.desc: _check_interrupt() — checked again after the validation loop completes

execute_tools.name: Settings → Agent
execute_tools.desc: Tool is dispatched to its handler; result streamed back to the loop

db_persist_tool.name: Settings → Source
db_persist_tool.desc: Tool result (role=tool) is persisted to the interactions table

delegation_chk.name: Settings → Agent
delegation_chk.desc: If result contains __delegate__ key, agent switches mid-loop and rebinds session

skill_track.name: Settings → Source
skill_track.desc: skill_track_execution + skill_get_rating run after every tool result

check_continue.name: Settings → Max Turns
check_continue.desc: Configure the maximum number of agentic turns per request

final_response.name: /optimize
final_response.desc: Trigger optimizer on this session to improve future responses

db_persist_final.name: Settings → Source
db_persist_final.desc: Final assistant response is saved to the interactions table

memory_save.name: Settings → Source
memory_save.desc: View and manage memory and context documents

opt_collect.name: /optimize [feedback]
opt_collect.desc: Trigger a new optimizer run against the current session

opt_collect.name: Settings → Optimizer
opt_collect.desc: Configure run mode, intensity, schedule, and scan scope

user_input.desc: Entry point for user-facing agents. The user's message arrives here — plain text from the chat UI, Telegram, email, or other channel.

details.val: user_input
Plain text string from the user
Web chat, Telegram, email, webhook, SMS

slash_cmd.desc: Checks the message against _OPTIMIZE_PATTERN. If matched, routes directly to the optimizer session — the main agent loop never runs.

details.val: _OPTIMIZE_PATTERN regex — catches /optimize and variants
Session rewritten to optimizer; main loop bypassed entirely
Falls through to ensure_session

ensure_session.desc: _ensure_session() — creates a new session row in the DB if none exists, or validates the provided session_id.

details.val: sessions
session_id, user_id, agent_id, created_at

agent_resolve.desc: Loads the agent record from the agents table. Determines which agent template, system prompt, tools, and max_turns apply.

details.val: agents
agent_id, system_prompt, bootstrap_tools, max_turn_count, model, temperature

participants.desc: Enforces participant access rules — verifies the user is permitted to interact with this agent before any work begins.

details.val: user_id present in agent participants list
Request rejected before any DB writes or loop execution

save_user_msg.desc: Inserts the user's message as role="user" into the interactions table — the source-of-truth record for this turn.

details.val: interactions
user
Before the agent loop — always written even if the agent errors out

load_context.desc: Queries the agents table for context documents to inject into the system prompt. Each column maps to a named section.

details.val: agent_prompt, user_prompt, skills_prompt, tasks_prompt, misc_prompt, system_prompt
AGENT IDENTITY · USER · SKILLS · TOOLS · TASKS · MEMORY · PROJECT

copy_defaults.desc: On the agent's first run, copies context documents from the default template so the agent has a working starting configuration.

details.val: No existing context rows found for this agent
Default agent template (agents table defaults)

skip_gate.desc: _should_skip_memory() — trivial or short messages (greetings, single commands) skip memory_search entirely to save latency.

details.val: Regex match on message length and content
memory_search bypassed; brain_context = None
Continues to memory_search normally

memory_search.desc: Semantic search over the agent's memory pages to find relevant facts from past sessions. Results injected into the system prompt as [BRAIN CONTEXT].

details.val: memory_search (internal — stripped from history shown to LLM)
# [BRAIN CONTEXT] section in system prompt
No brain context injected; pipeline continues normally

resolve_attach.desc: Resolves attachment IDs into file metadata. Prepares a [USER ATTACHMENTS] section so the agent knows what files were uploaded.

details.val: attachments table by attachment_id list
# [USER ATTACHMENTS] — name, mime_type, size, attachment_id
read_attachment — agent uses this to fetch file content

attachment_describe.desc: When the model handling the turn can't see images, a separately-configured vision model describes each attached image once and the description is injected into the user message (and persisted, so later turns keep it). Active only on turns where it actually runs.

details.val: An image is attached AND no selected text model is image-capable
The image describer chosen in App Config → Default LLM (per-model Image capability)
[Attached image — <name>]: <description> into the user message
Per-agent on/off; skip for agents that never handle images

build_prompt.desc: build_system_prompt() — assembles all context sections, brain context, and bootstrap tools into a single system prompt string.

details.val: [AGENT DIRECTIVE] → [AGENT IDENTITY] → [USER] → [SKILLS] → [TOOLS] → [TASKS] → [BRAIN CONTEXT]
context docs + memory results + agent.system_prompt + bootstrap_tools

build_history.desc: build_openai_history_from_session() — fetches all prior interactions and converts to OpenAI message format. Strips internal tools from history.

details.val: memory_search, memory_save (internal — never forwarded to LLM)
assistant tool_calls from persisted [Tool calls: …] suffix
[{role:user/assistant/tool, content:…}, …]

load_provider.desc: Reads LLM provider config from the agent record and environment. Sets base_url, api_key, model, temperature, max_tokens.

details.val: agent.model, agent.temperature, agent.max_tokens, env OPENROUTER_API_KEY / BASE_URL
Runs the agent's default model; the chat user can switch it per conversation

load_tools.desc: Fetches tool definitions — built-in tools plus user skills — filtered by the agent's allowed_tools disabled list.

details.val: BUILTIN_TOOL_METADATA + skills table
agent.allowed_tools = list of disabled tool names
List of tool dicts: name, description, parameters schema

integration_status.desc: Checks which OAuth integrations are enabled for this agent and whether the user has connected them. Injects a summary into the system prompt so the agent knows which services are available — and can surface a connect link via check_oauth_connection() when the user needs to link an account.

details.val: agent_connections table (enabled OAuth providers) + auth_elements table (user tokens)
## Available Integrations block appended to system prompt (only when integrations exist)
Provider listed with connected account email
Provider listed with instruction to call check_oauth_connection(provider)
Agent calls check_oauth_connection() → returns clickable link → user completes OAuth in popup (same link as Integrations tab)

assemble_msgs.desc: Builds the final messages array for the LLM: system prompt at [0], conversation history at [1..N], current user message at [N+1].

details.val: {role: "system", content: system_prompt}
Prior session turns from build_history
{role: "user", content: current message + any attachment context}

interrupt_chk.desc: _check_interrupt() — checks for a cancellation or shutdown signal. Raises AgentInterrupted if set, which ends the stream.

details.val: 5× per turn: loop start, before LLM, in validation loop (per tool), after validation, in execution loop (per result)
Raises AgentInterrupted → stream ends cleanly

turn_counter.desc: Increments the turn counter and checks against max_turns. If the limit is reached, forces exit to final_response. 0 means unlimited (no turn ceiling) — the wall-clock cap is the backstop instead.

details.val: max_turns = agent.max_turn_count (0 = unlimited; new agents seed 9999)
Exits while loop → final_response (skipped entirely when unlimited)
When bounded, +1 block granted if user approves the permission_chk request

permission_chk.desc: At turn ≥ 11, injects a permission-request fragment asking the user if the agent may continue. Scans the last user message for approval.

details.val: turn_num >= 11
Scans user message for "yes", "continue", "proceed", etc.
max_turns extended by 10

build_tool_defs.desc: Converts the loaded tool list into the OpenAI tool_calls schema format consumed by the LLM.

details.val: [{type:"function", function:{name, description, parameters:{type:"object",properties:{…}}}}]
Tools loaded at load_tools stage

llm_call.desc: The actual streaming LLM call. Yields text chunks and/or tool_call deltas. Response determines whether routing or final output follows.

details.val: OpenRouter (or custom base_url from load_provider)
Server-sent event chunks yielded in real time to client
LLM may return tool_calls → db_persist_asst → validation → execution
LLM returns plain text → check_continue → final_response

db_persist_asst.desc: Saves the assistant's raw response as role="assistant" BEFORE validation runs. Appends a [Tool calls: …] JSON suffix listing requested tool calls.

details.val: interactions (role=assistant)
Appends \n\n[Tool calls: [{name, args}, …]] to content
Immediately after LLM response — before any tool is validated or executed

validate_tools.desc: _validate_tool_call() — for each requested tool call, checks the tool name exists and arguments are parseable. Invalid calls get an error result without executing.

details.val: Tool name in registry · args JSON-parseable · required params present
Returns validation error result; tool skipped
Validated in a for-loop; interrupt_chk runs each iteration

destructive_chk.desc: Checks if the requested tool is in the DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS set. These tools require explicit user confirmation before they can execute.

details.val: edit_source · write_source · delete_source · run_command · restart_server
Forwards to guardrails for confirmation check
Proceeds to post_val_chk then execution

guardrails.desc: _check_user_confirmed() — verifies the user explicitly approved the destructive action in their most recent message. Blocks execution if no confirmation.

details.val: Last user message for confirmation keywords
Tool proceeds to execution
Tool skipped; emits blocked event; jumps to check_continue

post_val_chk.desc: _check_interrupt() again after the full validation loop completes. Catches cancellations that arrived while tools were being validated.

details.val: After the per-tool validation for-loop, before execute_tools
Raises AgentInterrupted — no tools execute

execute_tools.desc: Dispatches each validated tool to its registered handler function. Streams the result back into the turn's tool_results list.

details.val: tool_name → handler lookup in tool registry
Collected into tool_results list for this turn
Execution errors are caught and returned as error results — never raised

db_persist_tool.desc: Saves each tool result as role="tool" in the interactions table. Includes execution metadata.

details.val: interactions (role=tool)
tool_name · tool_call_id · duration_ms · success · input_params · error_message

delegation_chk.desc: Checks if the tool result contains a __delegate__ key. If found, switches the active agent mid-loop and rebinds the session.

details.val: result contains __delegate__: {agent_id, session_id}
Session rebound · tools reloaded · new system prompt injected · loop continues
Proceeds normally to skill_track

skill_track.desc: After each tool result: looks up the skill by tool name, records the execution event, and updates the performance rating score.

details.val: skill_get_id_by_name → skill_track_execution → skill_get_rating
skill score in DB (used by optimizer to prioritize improvements)
Errors swallowed — skill tracking never fails the turn

check_continue.desc: Decides whether to loop back for another turn or proceed to final output. Tool results present = loop; no tool calls = stop.

details.val: tool_results non-empty → back to interrupt_chk for turn N+1
No tool calls in LLM response → proceed to final_response
max_turns reached → final_response regardless of tool results

final_response.desc: Streams the final assistant message to the client over WebSocket. This is the text the user sees.

details.val: Streamed as SSE chunks via WebSocket
LLM response text — tool call results already reflected in conversation history

db_persist_final.desc: Saves the final assistant response to the interactions table. Distinct from db_persist_asst — that saved mid-loop tool-calling turns; this saves the concluding message.

details.val: interactions (role=assistant)
On clean exit — interrupt and max_turns paths are handled earlier in the loop

memory_save.desc: The memory_save internal tool runs after the final response — extracts key facts from the session and upserts them into the agent's long-term memory store.

details.val: memory_save (internal — stripped from history shown to LLM)
brain / memory pages table
Skipped if the memory tool is disabled for this agent

opt_collect.desc: Triggered by a tool call from another agent — not by direct user input. Receives a structured JSON payload containing session_id, optional feedback, and scan scope.

details.val: tool_call
JSON: { session_id, feedback?, scope?, intensity? }
run_optimizer tool call · /optimize slash command
